Outcome: Depressive symptoms (lower is better)

## Study A
Found: benefit
Claim: Older adults in the second, third and fourth serum 25(OH)D quartiles had 18-22% lower depressive symptom scores than those in the lowest quartile.
Sentence: "Fully adjusted models indicated a 22 % (RR 0.78, 95 % CI 0.68-0.89), 21 % (RR 0.79, 95 % CI 0.68-0.90), and 18 % (RR 0.82, 95 % CI 0.71-0.95) lower score of depressive symptoms in people in the second, third, and fourth 25(OH)D quartiles, when compared to people in the first quartile (P for trend <0.0001)."
Measured as: depressive symptom score (15-point Geriatric Depression Scale)
Population: 2839 Dutch older adults aged 65 years and older
Intervention: Serum 25(OH)D concentration by quartile (observational exposure)
Comparator: Lowest 25(OH)D quartile
Design: cohort study
Sample size: 2,839
baseline_vitamin_d_status: not_reported

## Study B
Found: no effect
Claim: No direct association was found between vitamin D deficiency and depression symptoms.
Sentence: "No direct association was observed between vitamin D deficiency and AS or DS."
Measured as: depression symptoms (DS)
Population: Adults in a population-based sample (n=1637)
Intervention: Vitamin D deficiency (<20 ng/mL in healthy population or <30 ng/mL in at-risk groups), measured serum level
Comparator: Vitamin D sufficiency
Design: cross-sectional study
Sample size: 1,637
baseline_vitamin_d_status: mixed

content.text: {"rationale":"Both observational studies bear on vitamin D and depressive symptoms but disagree, with differences in age group, exposure definition (quartiles vs deficiency cut-offs), and design; the population (older adults vs general adults) is the most likely explanation.","verdict":"genuine","reason":"population","also_differs":["intervention","design_or_bias","outcome_measure"],"detail":"population: Dutch adults 65+ vs a general adult population sample; exposure quartiles vs deficiency threshold"}
